correctness.rationale: A hypothetical friend n satisfies 5sigma(n)=9n and 5|n. If 2|n, 10|n contradicts strict abundancy monotonicity; since sigma(n) odd, n is a square. If 3|n, squarefull 3 and 5 with exponents >=2 plus inequalities I(3^4 5^2)=3751/2025>9/5 and I(3^2 5^4)=10153/5625>9/5 force exponents exactly 2, after which 13,31|sigma(n) forces 13^2 31^2|n, contradicting I(3^2 5^2 13^2 31^2)=20191/10075>9/5. Thus v3(sigma(n))=2. For p=2 mod3 with even a, sigma(p^a)=1 mod3, while for p=1 mod3 LTE gives v3(sigma(p^a))=v3(a+1). Taking v3 of the product yields sum exactly 2 and its partitions 2 or 1+1. Congruence arithmetic gives singleton a mod54 in {8,44}, two-carrier a mod18 in {2,14}, others mod6 in {0,4}. Independently checked the exact rational inequalities and 200 local prime-power valuations. No hypothetical friend was constructed; no conclusion about existence.

originality.rationale: Ward (2008) proves odd-square/non-3-divisibility, 9|sigma(n), at least one carrier exponent 2 mod6 and a weaker singleton 8 mod18, but does not claim at most two carriers or exact v3 budget and modulo-54 dissection. Mandal (2025) proves a different restriction on half-exponents. The refinement uses an immediately available Ward equation plus standard LTE; it is close to a classical lemma and could be implicit in Ward's proof, a serious novelty risk. Nevertheless the precise all-carrier allocation is not a theorem implied by Ward's stated weaker congruences alone.
residual_risks: The result is very close to a one-step LTE refinement of the exact 3-adic budget implicit in Ward's 2008 proof; may have been recognized without being separately written.
No friend of 10 is known; the statement is conditional and only a necessary exponent sieve, not a construction or proof of solitude.
The modest extra strength may be subsumed in weakly indexed literature or a published factor-chain algorithm; originality and value are bounded accordingly.

value.rationale: The existence of a friend of 10 is unresolved and numerical/factor-chain attempts naturally sieve prime-power exponent patterns. The exact total 3-adic budget limits all 1-mod-3 exponent carriers to one or two and removes an entire allowed residue of Ward's singleton condition. This is a limited but concrete reusable necessary condition, not a claimed solution or a newly invented arbitrary modulus. Because the algebraic refinement is elementary, its marginal utility rather than broad novelty is emphasized.

scientific_limitations: All conclusions are conditional on existence of n≠10 with sigma(n)/n=9/5.
Only the 3-adic exponent allocation is constrained; there is no assertion about all p-adic factors or absolute nonexistence.
